page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / You cannot be serious!
title: You cannot be serious!
description:
Mr Socrates, the big boss from America, is in town and everything must be just right. Unfortunately the hotel room Anna booked for him isn't right so it's up to her to sort it out and that involves some complaining.
This episode focuses on the language to use when things aren't right and you need to complain.
phrases: I'm very disappointed with your service.
The standard of service is not good enough.
The room I booked did not meet my expectations.
I would like this matter resolved as quickly as possible,
I would like to cancel my reservation and get a full refund.

listening_challenge.question: What type of hotel room did Mr Socrates want?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to Tip Top Trading where everyone seems a bit flustered.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: …and we really need the best biscuits there are.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes, and I’ve made sure there’s tea and coffee…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: …and the carpets?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Uh?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: …have they been cleaned.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Don’t panic Paul, all taken care of.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You see, the big boss from America, Mr Socrates, is in town and everything must be just right. What’s he like Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, so far he seems OK. A bit bossy, quite short and… a bit smelly!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, he did just fly in from the States. But you booked him into a good hotel so hopefully he’s had a chance to clean up.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I hope so! Oh, I had better get that. Hello? Ah hello Mr Socrates, did you sleep well? Oh! I see… I see… erm… well… oh, I don’t know… Tom said it was five-star… well… OK… goodb- Oh, he’s hung up.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Everything OK Anna? You look a bit pale.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It was Mr Socrates. He’s not happy.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Golly gosh, oh dear. What’s the matter?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It’s his hotel room. He doesn’t like it. The bed’s too soft, too small and it’s a single room not a twin room.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh yes, he likes to have two beds in the room for some reason.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But Tom said he only likes a single bed in the room.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Really? Oh no, he insists on a twin – something to do with business partners he says. Anything else?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. He says he wanted freshly squeezed orange juice for breakfast, not the stuff out of a carton.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Anything else?! A view of Mount Everest perhaps?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, thank you Denise. Well, we really must sort this out. We can’t afford to upset Mr Socrates. Now Anna, you chose this hotel, I really think you need to sort out this mess.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It was Tom’s suggestion…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Just sort it, quickly. Oh golly gosh, golly gosh.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Uh oh Anna. Time to do some complaining. What are you going to say?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh... I don’t know. I’m not very good at complaining.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Well, Anna. Keep your cool and politely tell the hotel why you’re not happy. You could say:
I’m very disappointed with your service.
The standard of service is not good enough.
The room I booked did not meet my expectations
Good luck Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK. Here goes.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Hello. Royal Imperial Hotel.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Erm... hello… I want to… I want to complain.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Really? About what exactly?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Your hotel… Well, I mean, a room I booked for my boss. Room 101. I’m very disappointed with your service.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: And why’s that then?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, the room isn’t like the one I booked. It’s just not good enough.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Hmm. Let’s have a look at the booking… well your boss got a bed… and breakfast too… a continental breakfast in fact.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But the room just didn’t meet his expectations… hello?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Give me the phone Anna, I’ll deal with this. Now hello Miss…?

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Miss Fit.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Miss Fit? This is the office assis- I mean Manager here. This isn’t good enough. My colleague has made it quite clear that the room did not meet our requirements and I would like you to resolve this matter as quickly as possible or I will have to cancel our reservation.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Sadly, we have no other twin rooms available and anyway…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Alright, I’d like to speak to your manager please. Really!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Good old Denise. I can tell she’s done this before but will talking to the manager really sort things out? Let’s remind ourselves of some of the phrases you can use when you need to complain:
I’m very disappointed with your service.
The standard of service is not good enough.
The room I booked did not meet my expectations.
And to get things sorted you could say:
I would like this matter resolved as quickly as possible.
Or:
I would like to cancel my reservation and get a full refund.
Let’s see if Denise has sorted things out?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So have you managed to sort out Mr Socrates?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh yes, Anna’s got him a new room.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Thanks Anna, I’ll let him know. And what about the orange juice?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Errr…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Freshly squeezed, every morning!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh golly gosh, that reminds me, we need some here in the office. He’s going to be here any minute and he says he’s got some important news for us.
